analogy.name: A coat-check room
analogy.line: A HashMap is like a coat check: the ticket number (hash) picks the rack, and on that rack you compare tags (equals) to find your exact coat.

java-core.caption: A hash picks the bucket and equals picks the key. A bad hash piles keys into one bucket and turns O(1) lookups into O(n).
steps: The ticket number is the hash. Real name: hashCode of the key. Equal keys must give equal hashes, the contract interviewers test.
The rack is the bucket. Real name: the hash chooses a slot. Good hashes spread keys evenly, bad ones pile them onto one rack.
Comparing tags is equals. Real name: inside the bucket, equals finds the exact key. Hash alone is never enough.
Handing over the coat is the value returned. Real name: a collision only means a short walk along one rack, not a broken map.

analogy.name: A warehouse with a sorting belt
analogy.line: The heap is like a warehouse: new parcels arrive at the loading dock (Eden), most are thrown out quickly, and the few that stay are moved to long-term shelves (old generation).

jvm.caption: New objects land in Eden and most die young. Survivors age into the old generation, where collections are rare and expensive.
steps: The office archive is Metaspace. Real name: class data and methods live here, not your objects, so a leak here is a class-loading problem.
The loading dock is Eden. Real name: new objects start here and a minor GC sweeps it, since most objects die young.
Survivors move to long-term shelves. Real name: they age through S0 and S1 into the old generation, where a full GC is rare and costly.

analogy.name: A hotel front desk
analogy.line: A request through Spring is like a hotel stay: the front desk (DispatcherServlet) routes you, the concierge (controller) takes your ask, the manager (service) decides, and the archive clerk (repository) files it.

spring.caption: One front door, then layers: controller maps, service decides, repository persists. Business rules live in the service and nowhere else.
steps: The front desk is the DispatcherServlet. Real name: every request enters here and is handed to the right handler.
The concierge is the controller. Real name: it maps the route and reads the request, with no business rules inside.
The manager is the service. Real name: business rules and the transaction boundary live here, where the decisions are made.
The archive clerk is the repository. Real name: it talks to the database in domain terms, not raw SQL strings.
The archive room is the database. Real name: durable storage, and the repository is the only box allowed to know how it works.

analogy.name: An assembly line
analogy.line: A Maven build is like an assembly line: each station runs every earlier station first, so asking for the finished product already means inspected and tested.

java-build.caption: Maven phases run in order and each runs everything before it. package already compiled and tested; you do not run them separately.
steps: The first station checks the blueprint. Real name: validate. Is the POM, the plugin setup and the project shape sound?
The second station cuts parts. Real name: compile turns source into bytecode. A failure here is a language error, not a build error.
The third station inspects. Real name: test runs the suite. A failing test stops the line before anything is packaged.
The fourth station boxes the product. Real name: package makes one jar from what was just tested, the proof of the build.
The last station ships to the store room. Real name: install puts the jar in the local repository for other modules to use.
